summary.text: Gloria Mendoza is a Republican member of the Washington House of Representatives for District 14-Position 1, in office since January 13, 2025, and she is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Democrat Chelsea Dimas.
A business owner and former mayor of Grandview, she describes herself as a Mexican immigrant and former farmworker.

paragraphs.text: Mendoza was born in Mexico and moved to Grandview, Washington, at age eight, according to Wikipedia.
She graduated from Grandview High School and attended Yakima Valley College.

Her House Republican biography says she worked as an employment and training manager for a nonprofit before starting her own business, and that she is CEO and founder of GMC Training Institute, a vocational school that opened in 1999, and founder of GMC Family Services.

Mendoza joined the Grandview City Council in 2013 and was appointed mayor in December 2018 to finish the term of Norm Childress, who had resigned; she won a full term in 2019 and lost her 2023 re-election bid to Ashley Lara.
She is active in the Rotary Club, the Grandview Chamber of Commerce and the Main Street Grandview Association.
After court-ordered redistricting moved Republican Chris Corry out of the 14th District, Mendoza ran for Position 1 in 2024 and defeated Democrat Chelsea Dimas, 54 percent to 45 percent.
Her biography lists her priorities as protecting individual rights, bringing jobs to the district, opposing new taxes and regulations, and helping small businesses.
